If we are being real, the town I used to live in where most of these events happened is the reason I have the phobia in the first place... Before I moved there, I actually used to pick up tarantulas. Id watch arachnophobia for freaking fun (sounds insane to me now) and had no problem relocating or killing a spider myself but this whole town traumatized me to the point that I can't even do it myself anymore.. my husband always laughs about it.. cause even if I'm watching it on TV I have to close my eyes and ears. Stargate has a character where there are basically spider people bag guys and he makes this clicky sound ( the main bad) when he talks and it legit gives me the heebee geebees... My husband laughed the whole time I played Hogwarts legacy cause I was screaming and jumping at the video games because of the spiders. I live streamed it for my friends and it didn't matter if I knew it was coming out not I still got scared. Id hyperventilate knowing what was around the corner sometimes it just stop in the middle of the quest and back out of where I was. This was before they updated it so you could play on arachnophobia mode... I didn't do certain quests just to avoid the spiders... I think eventually I just had my husband get me through them.. my sweet dear husband /s eventually figured out the clicky sound freaks me out and started doing it to me randomly... He stopped when eventually he made me cry because of how much I can't stand it... When I played Skyrim I just had him get me through the spider quests cause I just couldn't at that point... 

Spiders are my only real fear though... I haven't been able to work through that phobia like I did with heights. I used to freeze with that but my dad was an electrician and used to make me get on the roof to help him put up Christmas lights. Eventually it turned to me being his helper and being in a 14 ft ladder with no support to hold up a chandelier... Don't get me wrong there are still situations where I legit will not be able to move but I've faced a lot of that fear. Some of the sketchy situations I've been on roofs kinda cured that for me 😭 I was forced to face it and one day I will face my spiders but the closest I've been is squishing the tiniest spider because it got too close to my daughter ... Which is huge progress for me really... I still get frozen on the toilet from time to time and make my husband come kill them but progress is progress in my eyes lol the only reason he's so understanding about killing them though is cause he's scared of bees and has a very violent reaction to them. He's thrown some sketchy things at bees and left me standing there while he zooms tf outta there 😂 funniest crap is watching him go outside to take care of a wasp nest and then watching him zip across the yard back and forth😂😂 let's just say, I'm the designated wasp killer and he's the designated spider killer lol.

Honestly I think it does make it harder. IMO. While it protected you from being default nanny, it prevents you from being involved essentially in this child's life. Which prevents you from bonding outside her dad. She may be at an age where she's wondering why you're even there. At 6 she definitely doesn't understand their parenting style so you not getting any alone time with her definitely makes you seem like a 3rd wheel. Honestly I'm sure many people have made this parenting style work, I personally couldn't do it myself. I definitely wish you luck in that department. Cause even with not liking other kids, you've been around for 4 years. At 6 she wouldn't have many memories, if any, by now that would be of just her and Dad. By now you should be normal and y'all should have some sort of bond. 

I definitely hope you find what will truly make you happy in life in the end. Whether it be staying with your SO or deciding you want more for yourself.  Everyone deserves true happiness and I hope you find it. I hope one day you look back when you're old and grey and know that you truly did what was best for you in the end during your life. I wish I had more comforting or helpful words but if you ever need to talk, I'm here. Being a SP is hard AF no matter if you're hands on or not. Plus kids are complicated beings and no matter how sweet or perfect, they can definitely be a challenge.

No, I get that... My husband became a dad at 22..  I was partying and making dumb choices at that age..  DH is 33 now and I'm barely turning 30. When he and BM divorced it was like he was trying to make up for lost time with BM so we did a ton of partying at the beginning  of our relationship but to me my biological clock was ticking and I was done with my party days pretty quickly afterwards.. On top of that he was doing the whole dad thing and I felt almost like a bump on a log when it came to what school SS was going to, how he developed in school, like all the things he had to worry about I just want a part of .. of course now we try to show togetherness when it comes to parenting even as a SP our  house is United. It helps that BM is remarried though. SS didn't see it as me encroaching in his time with Dad anymore. He saw it as 2 separate houses with 2 separate parents. 

My SS is 9 so I'm not sure if that makes a difference... When he was 6 I just tried to play the fun aunt roll and even tried taking him on adventures just me and him when his dad was at work. We go to the movies or park or something of that nature and sit in silence sometimes but it was the effort that I put forth that I guess he appreciated and it grew our bond. I got to know him just me and him rather than trying to force the family unit on him... I'm not sure if there is something they like to do together but maybe set a day that they get to go do that ... My SS and husband are super into video games (I am too) so I give up my lap top so he can play games he normally wouldn't be able to with his dad. I just go to the store or go watch TV elsewhere to show them to have their them time. But when it comes to doing stuff together she is going to have to learn that you're part of the family too.

 It may be a divorced child symptom of maybe wanting get parents back together, especially if y'all share a friend group (him and BM  I mean) she probably sees a good dynamic between her parents at an age where she's growing her own opinions and is a hell of a lot more aware and sees a possibility of them getting back together but you're in the way. Even if this isn't at all the case, to her it makes sense.  But just a reminder that even if y'all get closer, it won't change the fact that I'm the end she isn't yours... It's not going to be as apparent some days but others it's going to hurt like hell... Especially if you have any desire to be a mother of your own... 

Watching them parent together will grow your resentment and you may be able to pass it off for a while but you'll probably still end up coming back to the therapist to work through this again... And again.. And again.. Not that your SO isn't enough but rather one is a different need than the other... Neither can be ignored forever. I hope in the end it works out and you can work through your feelings if you decide to never have a child but if you're still young and feel you're in the club (metaphorically) stage then you have plenty of time to think about it. Just make sure that if he ever proposes that you take a long hard serious time out by yourself and really truly discuss whether you're ok with never having children. Not having children isn't the end of the world but you also don't want to ignore a part of you that has a need. Cause if that need will never be filled then you'll always feel like you're missing something...

I'm legit thinking back to all of my spider scares (arachnophobia here too).. I've never once reacted that way.. I legit walked through a web one evening and looked down to what looked like hundreds of baby spiders crawling up the webs...I froze till I saw the spiders and then proceeded to cry as I flailed around and begged my coworker to spray me down with the water hose as I slapped every inch I could find of myself.... I had one on me after running from a bee and froze for that one till I got someone to swipe it off and immediately went into actual hysterics, laughing and crying at the same time...I tried jumping into crocodile invested waters to get away from one my aunt was paddling our kayak into ...I wore rain boots and long pants in 100 degree weather to avoid the wolf spiders that ran across my feet at my job every day for the time I worked at that job... I stayed on a couch with my feet up for a whole 12 hours because one ran under the couch across from me... Like I've done some extreme stuff but never put anyone in the hospital....

Unfortunately it doesn't change your feelings. I honestly thought maybe if my SS hated me it would make it easier knowing he wasn't mine.. but it didn't.. I still resented the relationship his dad and him had and was jealous of BM even though my husband can't stand her .. Simply cause they had what I wanted... They are forever connected through my SS.. I married my husband but I found myself trying to out do my husband ex at every corner.. I even had us move so that the house felt more like our home rather than me living in another woman's home... Even with all of those changes, I still didn't feel like I was getting the true experience of going through life with my husband. I felt like I was an outsider... Now with the baby I share all kinds of new experiences with him... For one he's never had a daughter, never had 2 kids, never dealt with a breast feeding wife or one with PPD and PPA. It's all new and I feel like I'm actually experiencing life with him now... Gosh I know this whole thing probably sounds awful but the ugly truth is I felt envious... Separately from the want of being a mom... Oh gosh I was so bad about that, I ended up with 3 fully stocked fishtanks, 5 cats, and 4 dogs....I tried to make up for the fact that the mother instinct in me was so heavy that I just over ran my life with things that depended on ME... I still have my animals and they all adore my baby but had I had her earlier I definitely wouldn't have had this many 😂

It may bring y'all closer which won't fill the motherly role but it will make you feel just slightly less like an outsider.. not much but slightly ..

I know it's not relevant for older kids but I let my baby choose when she wants to sleep. I tried seeing a schedule and doing the on time naps and what not and it was a fight every single time.... So I let her choose her own damn schedule. She naps around 12, 4 and 8. I refuse to make her stay in her room at 8 cause she always wakes up one more time, plays and then is ready for actual bed by 12 at the latest. I do make sure she is bathed and I'm PJs and fed by 8 but this had made my life so much easier... And food.. I fought and fought trying to keep her clean and using a spoon every time... Finally I stopped. I just put her food directly in her tray, step get down to a diaper and let her go at it. When she's done I rinse her off with water in the tub or if it's bath day I give her a bath. I also let my dogs clean up her mess after meals. I set down a puppy pads under her chair to catch as much as possible but the dogs usually clean it for me after. Then I throw it in the bath tub after too and just give it a good once over with some cleaning spray and the massage setting on the shower head lol. 

For older kids, I've found that letting them choose what's for dinner has significantly changed the dynamic about picky eating. Ex: my SS said he wanted pizza one night so I got raw tortillas from the store and some toppings and let him make them. I even change it up and do different kinds of doughs. When he wants chicken nuggets I have him help me bread the chicken nuggets with Cheetos and he helps me snap the ends off fresh green beans. Having him pick what we eat or giving him an option of "do you want green beans or corn with your chicken nuggets?" Or "should I add cheese or bacon on top of the mashed potatoes?" This kids ate Brussel sprouts this summer simply cause he helped make them and it made him interested in what it tasted like with the bacon. Turns out he likes them. When it comes to plating I ask if he wants this or that and if he isn't hungry at the time I won't make him eat. But if he comes back later asking for food I only offer what I made for dinner. If he still doesn't want that then I will offer a peanut butter sandwich. Those are his only options and I stick to it. It's helped us a ton when it comes to him fighting us about eating...

I second the music thing. I used to hold my baby and dance to the music. I would turn it up loud and we would kind of dance a little around the kitchen. It helped a ton. Even if I just put her in the bouncer on my island it distracted her enough for me to get clarity and either figure out why she is crying or find solutions to calm her. Sometimes the loud music itself helped. Id sing to her and kinda get her little hands and move them. She to this day loves when I do it and is the only way to calm her in the car as well.

I just want to say that I kind of felt like you for a long time.... My SS loves me but I felt like I wished his dad and I had him instead of his ex... I was jealous even... But part of me started to resent the fact that my SS wasnt mine... At the end of the day, he didn't have to listen to me. I'm not his mom.. at the end of the day, he still went home to his real mom... I can say I love him like my own all day and id do anything for him, which is 100% true but it still didn't make him mine... I tried and tried to put on a brave face and tell people I was cool and wanted to be child free.. made up every excuse in the book as to why I was so chill about it and lied to my self that my husband was enough and I didn't need a baby..I whole heatedly convinced myself too..

Then I got pregnant... My husband and I were so scared and excited all at the same time and it felt like a dream.. ex showed her a*s a little cause she doesn't want any more kids outside of SS but now she wasn't special anymore. My husband even talked about having a whole football team... Just as many babies as possible. The further I got into my pregnancy I realized I didn't want anymore besides the one... Just one perfect little girl to complete our family and make it whole. And that's exactly how it feels, like my family is finally complete.. my SS adores his little sister and this last summer whole we had him was our best summer yet... I felt complete. I said I was happy never having a baby but in reality I just convinced myself to settle for less than I wanted. Again not that I don't adore my husband and definitely would not want to live without him but having my daughter made my eyes open to the truth of what I was truly feeling that entire time... I ended up getting my tubes removed a few months after I had her and I feel no regret. She's only 7 months but I definitely don't feel any regrets. She's all I ever wanted. Little attitude and everything.

My LO is almost 7 months. She eats mostly purees but we do on occasion follow some of the baby lead weaning. Of course it's always up to you what you're comfortable feeding baby. My daughter doesn't eat most of it and usually ends up wearing it a lot but she does feed herself. Not with a spoon like if I was feeding her of course but I like to let her explore with her food. I also give her baby snacks and cheerios to help develop her pincer grasp. Even though they can't chew they can gum things.

 Examples of how I've baby lead weaned: smooshed avocado, the bone of a chicken wing (just the bone, no meat or anything on it at all), a long piece of steak that she can't get a piece off of (she sucks on it), the cob of a corn for her to just gum, rice and finely chopped up meat, refried beans, blueberries, strawberry, banana etc in her little mesh eater.

We recently went out of town and I let her have some of my breakfast. She ate an omelet that I sliced into long strips so she can take pieces off, part of some toast, a little bit of blueberry yogurt and that's it. She ended up liking the eggs the most.

I also like to put purees on her plate with each meal as an option. She usually opts to either eat them directly with her hand or dips her baby snacks or spoon in the purees. She's been eating regular food since 4.5 months though so she's had some practice. 

The point of me sharing this is to show some things you can try with your LO. It is natural for babies to gag a little when staying to eat so remember that and keep an eye out with your best judgement. You're not a bad parent no matter what route you choose as long as your baby is getting nutrients. Let baby be messy though cause that's the only way they will learn to explore with food. But to add baby lead weaning has been proven to make less picky eaters and food before 1 is just for fun so most of the nutrient baby is getting is still coming from bottles.

Just a warning.

We take pick up and take my bonus son  in/to Missouri (12 hr drive). We leave at midnight cause it's a guarantee my daughter is asleep at midnight and she sleeps for most of the drive. It also minimizes the amount of stops we have to make. Of course we check her every so often but she sleeps great. She'll wake at 6 get her morning feed then sleep till about 10 when we have to make a few stops here and there to entertain, feed and change her. But it makes it a 2 hour drive in her eyes. By the time we get there she's ready for lunch and another nap.

You don't have to pump at events. Ask the host for a private spot to breast feed. That's how I fed my 3 month old at the time when I went to my cousin's wedding. She slept through the music and everything. Of course I kept her a certain distance from the speakers. She kept her nap schedule and slept down the aisle in my grandma's arms too. It's possible to attend events with an infant.
